newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's National Front wants to be kingmaker.
newsitem.headline: France's National Front wants to be kingmaker.

text.p: France's far-right National Front aims to be kingmaker in the National Assembly and all its candidates in a position to do so will run in next Sunday's election second round, its deputy leader Bruno Megret said on Monday.

"What we want is to have a number of parliamentarians sufficient so that nothing can be done without us," Megret told France Inter radio. He said the Front could win up to 12 seats but admitted it could have none.
National Front candidates in about 100 constituencies polled 12.5 percent of registered voters, the required threshold to be allowed to stand in the run-off.

Megret said the National Front leadership would meet in the morning to look into its position for the run-off and it was not certain that the Front would give precise instructions to all its candidates.
"We'll look into it quietly. We have to translate into more precise instructions our objective which is to have deputies in a position to be kingmakers in the National Assembly," he said.

The Front's leader Jean-Marie Le Pen had called on voters before the first round to vote for the left to trip the ruling right. Megret declined to say who the Front would back but said: "We are quite opposed to the left".
